events.title: The death of Pope Pius IX
events.shortBlurb: The longest-reigning pope closed a stormy pontificate that defined the Immaculate Conception and saw the loss of the Papal States…
body: On 7 February 1878 Pope Pius IX died after nearly thirty-two years on the throne of Peter, the longest reign in the history of the papacy after St. Peter himself. His pontificate defined the dogma of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary in 1854 and convoked the First Vatican Council of 1869–1870, which proclaimed the pope’s infallibility in matters of faith and morals.

In the same years the movement for Italian unity stripped away the Papal States and seized Rome itself in 1870, so that Pius IX spent his last years calling himself the “prisoner of the Vatican.” Long venerated for his personal piety, he was beatified in 2000 by Pope John Paul II.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Beatification of Pope Pius IX (vatican.va)
